title: Aamir Khan Just Reunited Three of Bollywood's Greatest. The Film Is About India's First Win Over Pakistan.
excerpt: Twenty-five years after Lagaan, Aamir and Ashutosh Gowariker return to cricket. Rajkumar Hirani produces. The Dangal writers wrote the script. And Farhan Akhtar might be co-starring.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Aamir Khan's new film 'Lalkaara' focuses on India's first cricket victory over Pakistan in 1952.
  • The film features a powerhouse team: Aamir Khan, Ashutosh Gowariker, and Rajkumar Hirani.
  • Production is set to begin in October 2026, with a focus on themes of rivalry and friendship.
  • Lalkaara is not a biopic but a sports drama exploring partition and nationalism.
  • Aamir Khan chose this project over the long-awaited '3 Idiots' sequel due to a ready script.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ll4uIeAA2IY Some announcements land like gossip. This one lands like a lineup card. **Aamir Khan** is making a film called **Lalkaara**. It's about the 1952 Test series between India and Pakistan — India's first-ever series victory against their fiercest rivals. **Ashutosh Gowariker** is directing. **Rajkumar Hirani** is producing. **Farhan Akhtar** and **Ritesh Sidhwani's** Excel Entertainment are co-producing. The script was written by **Piyush Gupta**, who wrote *Dangal*, and **Neeraj Singh**, who wrote *Nil Battey Sannata*. ![Ashutosh Gowariker — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Ashutosh_Gowariker_at_the_launch_of_T_P_Aggarwal%27s_trade_magazine_%27Blockbuster%27_15.jpg) Read that paragraph again. It's not a rumour sheet. It's the most loaded creative roster in Hindi cinema assembled under one title. ## The Story Lalkaara draws from one of Indian cricket's most emotionally charged chapters. In 1952, barely five years after Partition tore the subcontinent in half, India and Pakistan faced each other in a Test series for the first time. Leading India was **Lala Amarnath** — the country's first Test captain, a man born in Lahore who crossed the border during Partition and rebuilt his life and career on the other side. > **"It's about the 1952 Test series between India and Pakistan — India's first-ever series victory against their fiercest rivals."** Aamir plays Amarnath. The film, according to sources close to the production, is "not a biopic but a sports drama that explores the themes of rivalry, friendship, partition, and nationalism." The 1952 series is the backdrop. The beating heart, reportedly, is the friendship between two men whose world was split in two — and who met again on a cricket field. If that sounds like it was reverse-engineered to make you cry, well, look at who's writing it. ![Rajkumar Hirani — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/44/Rajkumar_Hirani_2014.jpg) ## The Dream Team Every name on this project carries weight. Aamir and Ashutosh Gowariker last worked together on **Lagaan** in 2001. That film — a cricket epic set in colonial India — earned an Oscar nomination and became one of the defining cultural artifacts of Indian cinema. Twenty-five years later, they're going back to the pitch. Same actor-director pair. Same sport. Completely different era, completely different stakes. > "Lalkaara is not a biopic but based on the iconic 1952 test series between India and Pakistan. The script is said to be an intense sports drama which explores the theme of rivalry, friendship, partition and nationalism." — Source to Bollywood Hungama Rajkumar Hirani coming on board as producer is significant. His last two films with Aamir — **3 Idiots** and **PK** — are among the highest-grossing Hindi films ever made. He's not directing this one (he's reportedly saving that for the long-gestating 3 Idiots sequel), but his creative fingerprints are all over it. Sources say the story originated with Hirani, with "strong creative inputs from him and Abhijat Joshi on the screenplay." ![Bollywood Hungama — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/f/fd/Bollywoodhungamascreenshot.jpg) And then there's Farhan Akhtar. Reports suggest he's in advanced talks to co-star as Amarnath's closest friend — the friendship that anchors the narrative. Aamir and Farhan haven't shared a screen together since... well, ever. But Aamir's first film after Lagaan was Farhan's directorial debut, **Dil Chahta Hai**, another film that became a generational touchstone.

Excel Entertainment producing, Hirani producing, Gowariker directing, the Dangal writer scripting, and Aamir starring. If Farhan locks in, this is five different strands of Bollywood royalty converging on one film. ## Why the Diaspora Should Care This isn't just a cricket film. It's a Partition film. It's a friendship film. It's about the first time two newly born nations — nations made of people who were neighbours five years earlier — competed against each other on the world's stage. For the Indian diaspora, especially those with Punjab roots, Lala Amarnath's story is foundational. He was born in Lahore. He played club cricket there. He crossed the border during Partition, captained the new India, and led them to victory against a team full of men he once shared dressing rooms with. Production is expected to begin in October 2026. Aamir reportedly chose Lalkaara over the 3 Idiots sequel because the bound script was ready while the sequel's scripting is still underway. In a Bollywood landscape dominated by sequels, remakes, and franchise extensions, Lalkaara feels like something rarer — an original story about a real moment, made by people who've proven they know how to turn sport into cinema and history into feeling. The last time Aamir Khan played cricket in a movie, it changed Indian cinema. Nobody's saying that twice. But nobody's ruling it out either.
